{{short description|American university teacher}}
'''Lillian Hartman Hoddeson''' (born 20 December 1940, in New York City)<ref>birth data from the biographical entry in the book by Hoddeson ''et al.'' ''The Rise of the Standard Model''; other biographical data from Hoddeson ''et al.'' ''Out of the Crystal Maze''</ref> is an American historian of science, specializing in the history of physics and technology during the 2nd half of the 20th century.

==Education and career==
Hoddeson received in 1957 a high school diploma from the [[Bronx High School of Science]], in 1961 a bachelor's degree in physics from [[Barnard College]], and in 1966 a Ph.D. in physics from [[Columbia University]] with a dissertation on solid-state physics. She was an assistant professor of physics from 1967 to 1970 at Barnard College and from 1971 to 1976 at [[Rutgers University]]. In 1974–1975 she was a visiting fellow at [[Princeton University]] and took [[Thomas Kuhn]]'s "History of Quantum Mechanics" graduate course.<ref>[http://www.fnal.gov/pub/today/archive/archive_2011/today11-10-24_Lillian%20HoddesonReadMore.html Fermilab Historian Lillian Hoddeson wins APS prize, 24 October 2011, Fermilab Today]</ref> From  1977 to 1992 she held various academic positions at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]], before becoming there an associate professor from 1993 to 2000 and a full professor from 2000 until her retirement. Since 1978 she has held the position of [[Fermilab]]'s historian.

Hoddeson is the co-author or editor of several books and has published more than 50 articles in referred journals.<ref>[http://news.illinois.edu/blog/view/6367/206585 Lillian Hoddeson named to History of Science Chair at Illinois, 6 August 2007, U. of Illinois News Bureau]</ref> Her publications include a biography of [[John Bardeen]], history of the development of the transistor, history of Fermilab, technical history of the beginning of [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]], and history of the development of the atomic bomb in the [[Manhattan Project]]. She co-authored three important books on the history of particle physics and a 2015 book on the [[Superconducting Super Collider]].

In 2012 she received the [[Abraham Pais Prize for History of Physics]] from the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>[http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Hoddeson&first_nm=Lillian&year=2012 2012 Abraham Pais Prize in History Recipient, American Physical Society website]</ref> She was a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] for the academic year 2000–2001<ref>[https://news.illinois.edu/blog/view/6367/208460 History professor wins Guggenheim Fellowship for work on UI physicist, 13 April 2000, U. of Illinois News Bureau]</ref> and is a Fellow of the American Physical Society.<ref>[http://cqd.eecs.northwestern.edu/people/awards/APS_Women_Fellows.pdf Women Fellows, APS Physics]</ref>

She was married to physicist [[Gordon Baym]] from 1981 to 1992.
